messages:
auditor_elaine: Hi team — we need concise, reproducible evidence that rotating the production KMS key preserves access to historical objects and that rotation events are tamper-evident. Please include control mapping to SOC 2.

nate: Short answer: envelope encryption (DEK wrapped by KEK). KEK rotation produces a new key version; prior versions are retained for decryption. This maps to SOC 2 CC6 (logical access) and CC7 (change management).

devops_lee: Artifacts we can provide: filtered CloudTrail events for kms.amazonaws.com (RotateKey, ReEncrypt, CreateKey), aws kms describe-key outputs, sample S3 object metadata showing DEK key id, sample decryption verification (hash + keyVersion), signed export manifest, and bucket object-lock settings screenshot.

compliance_bot: [automated] export job queued: s3://compliance-exports/4965432100/kms-rotation-evidence.tar.gz (job=ev-496543) :hourglass: 

auditor_elaine: Please include the exact commands used to produce the exports and a tiny sample event so we can reproduce. Also: how do you prove chain-of-custody?

nate: Example AWS commands we used (trimmed):
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=kms.amazonaws.com --start-time 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z --query 'Events[?contains(Resources[0].ResourceName, `alias/rdw-prod-kms`)]' > kms-events.json
aws kms list-keys --query 'Keys[].KeyId' > keyids.json
for id in $(cat keyids.json); do aws kms describe-key --key-id $id >> keys-describe.json; done

Sample CloudTrail event (trimmed): {"EventId":"e-rot123","EventName":"RotateKey","EventTime":"2025-06-10T05:12:00Z","Resources":[{"ResourceType":"AWS::KMS::Key","ResourceName":"alias/rdw-prod-kms"}],"Username":"kms-ops@redwood.com"}

aj: Chain-of-custody: we GPG-sign the exported tarball, enable S3 Object Lock (GOVERNANCE), and require MFA-delete on the bucket. The manifest contains SHA256 checksums, operator id, and job id. We also record the export job in an internal audit ledger (immutable entry).

devops_lee: Edge cases: manual rewrap/re-encrypt of DEKs with a different KEK could break decryption. Detection: object metadata stores DEK wrapping-key-id; we alert on CloudTrail ReEncrypt events when destinationKeyId != expected. We'll include a 24-month scan for unexpected ReEncrypt events in the bundle.

auditor_elaine: Good. One more: include a short 4-step example timeline showing how you'd tie a rotation event to forensic decryption of an archived object.

nate: Will include. ETA for bundle?

compliance_bot: [automated] export started: 2025-03-20T22:10:00Z ; estimated completion 10 minutes.

devops_lee: ETA ~12 minutes. I'll post S3 path + GPG signature here when done.

auditor_elaine: Thanks — will review when posted.
